what: Compounds (39 products, reagents, catalysts) have no kind and no structure. They became `other` and text. SMILES/InChI, CAS numbers and stereochemistry are the identity of a compound and are what a chemist would search on.
need: substances as definition kinds with structure identifiers
v0.39: partly resolved: products and substrate classes are `substance`; structures (SMILES, InChI, stereo) are for the synthesis extension

what: The scope is a table of compounds and yields. I collapsed it to ranges per class because one row per compound would need 39 definitions just to label rows. A compound table (structure, yield, dr, ee) is the core result of a methods paper.
v0.39: partly resolved: yields are ranges per class and overall; a table keyed by structures is for the synthesis extension

what: Reaction conditions (equivalents, mol%, solvent, concentration, temperature, light source, time) are a structured recipe; as text they cannot be compared across papers.
Yield kind matters: isolated vs crude NMR vs GC with internal standard. The variable's text carries it.
Selectivity (dr 1:1-1:1.2, E/Z, regioisomer ratio) is a ratio, not a number; the format has no ratio value.
proposal: extension: synthesis (core could add a ratio value, but only chemistry and genetics need it)
v0.39: open: ratios (dr 1:1.2) are still text; extension: synthesis, unless genetics or ecology need ratios too

what: Characterisation data (NMR spectra, HRMS, X-ray for 7') live in the ESI PDF. No availability level says 'in the supplement as images'; on_request is wrong, open is too strong. NMR FIDs would be the open data.
v0.39: resolved: `public` with a comment that it is supplementary information as images

what: Mechanistic evidence is a set of qualitative outcomes (allene formed, product not formed). Recorded as a boolean result; acceptable.
Each scope entry is a single run; replicates are not stated. The format cannot ask whether yields were reproduced.
proposal: extension: synthesis (the same field as wet-lab)
v0.39: extension: synthesis (shared with wet-lab: a core candidate)

what: There is no claim type for a reaction mechanism: `causal` was used. Mechanistic claims are the second kind of claim in synthesis and catalysis papers (and in biochemistry).
Failed substrates are the scope's boundary; the limitation category for 'the method does not work on X' had to be `sampling`. Negative scope entries deserve their own place.
The yield range 36-77% matches a table's min and max columns, but the validator checks numbers only against cells, and its unit-blind percent reading (see BUGS) also fails here.
v0.39: resolved: the range is a result {min 36, max 77}, and the percentage bug is fixed; no W17

what: Control experiments and routine mechanistic probes are not novel findings, yet novelty is required and has no 'not applicable' value; `extension` then asks for the work extended.
need: novelty not applicable to secondary claims
proposal: core (optional novelty for secondary claims, or a value not_applicable)

what: Type `mechanistic` fits; mechanism diagrams (catalytic cycles) are a figure the format can only reference.

Observation test: product characterisation (NMR, HRMS, an X-ray structure) is evidence of profile `observation` with records of kind `spectrum` and `structure`, supporting the scope claim through a supporting claim. Results say only that structures were assigned: per-compound spectra (shifts, m/z) are a table keyed by structures, for the synthesis extension.
